body.statement: For every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/4)\) and every admissible radius triple \( (r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in[0,\bar r]^3 \) for which \(\mathcal M_n\) is nonempty, a choice of \(K_{\alpha}\) depending only on the supplied radii and fixed class constants makes \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\in\mathcal I_n\) uniformly honest: \(\inf_{(P,m_0,m_1,p)\in\mathcal M_n}P\{\tau(P)\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\), with \(\sup_{\mathcal M_n}E_P[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha})]\le C_{\alpha}\rho_n\). Conversely every uniformly honest rule \(C_n\in\mathcal I_n\), including every rule using the public functions and certified radii, has worst-case expected length at least \(c_{\alpha}\rho_n\), so \(\mathfrak L_{n,\alpha}\asymp\rho_n\).
body.justification: It shows that honest expected length has the same four-channel rate as estimation risk.
body.gap: Published limited-overlap confidence and weak-overlap limit results do not calibrate this global-\(L^2\) minimax bias radius or prove its matching honest-length converse.
body.consumer: Applied work retaining the full population can report a bias-aware interval without invoking a Gaussian approximation in a bias-dominated regime.
body.proof_tex:
For \(n\geq5\), equation (73) verifies the premise of
\texttt{lem:median-risk-upgrade} uniformly, hence
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_n}P\{|
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{med}}-\tau(P)|>u\}
\leq\min\{1,10(K\rho_n/u)^3\}.                            \tag{81}
\]
For \(1\leq n<5\), \texttt{thm:clipped-absolute-upper} and
\(E_P|Z|\geq tP\{|Z|>t\}\) give
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_n}P\{|
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{med}}-\tau(P)|>C\rho_n/\alpha\}
\leq\alpha.                                               \tag{82}
\]
Choose \(K_\alpha\) at least \(K(10/\alpha)^{1/3}\) and at least the
finite-sample multiplier in (82).  Then
\[
\inf_{\mathcal M_n}P\{\tau(P)\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\}
\geq1-\alpha,\qquad
\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha})=2K_\alpha\rho_n. \tag{83}
\]
The center is measurable in \(O^{(n)}\), and its deterministic radius uses only
the supplied constants and certified radii.  Thus
\(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\in\mathcal I_n\), proving the honest expected-length
upper bound.

For the converse, take a two-point subexperiment from
\texttt{thm:four-channel-converse}, with targets separated by \(2d\) and sample
total variation at most \(\Gamma\).  Honesty at both fixed laws, transfer of an
event by the variational definition of total variation, and a union bound imply
under one law
\[
P\{\operatorname{length}(C_n)\geq2d\}
\geq1-2\alpha-\Gamma.                                     \tag{84}
\]
Indeed, on the intersection of the two transferred coverage events the
interval contains both targets.

For a fuzzy subexperiment, suppose its prior target is within \(d/4\) of
\(\mu_\theta\) except with prior probability \(\varepsilon\), the centers are
separated by \(2d\), and mixture total variation is at most \(\Gamma\).
Fixed-law honesty averaged under each prior says that the interval intersects
the corresponding \(d/4\)-neighborhood with probability at least
\(1-\alpha-\varepsilon\).  Transfer one event between mixtures and intersect
the two events.  An interval meeting both neighborhoods has length at least
\(3d/2\), so
\[
\overline P\{\operatorname{length}(C_n)\geq3d/2\}
\geq1-2\alpha-\Gamma-2\varepsilon.                        \tag{85}
\]
The two-point amplitudes can be chosen with \(\Gamma\leq1/4\); in each fuzzy
family, \(N\) can be enlarged until \(\Gamma+2\varepsilon\leq1/4\), without
changing membership or separation.  Since \(\alpha<1/4\), (84)--(85) have a
positive \(\alpha\)-dependent lower bound.  A mixture expectation averages
fixed-sign laws, every one of which lies in \(\mathcal M_n\), so some fixed law
has expected interval length at least a positive constant times \(d\).

Choose the largest component separation in (69).  Their sum is at most four
times their maximum, so \(d\geq c\rho_n\) after rescaling.  Every uniformly
honest \(C_n\in\mathcal I_n\) therefore satisfies
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_n}E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_n)]
\geq c_\alpha\rho_n.                                      \tag{86}
\]
Taking the infimum in \texttt{def:bias-aware-interval} and combining (83) with
(86) proves \(\mathfrak L_{n,\alpha}\asymp\rho_n\).  The lower bound has the
same reservoir-rich scope as the converse, while the interval upper bound uses
only the broader uniform-shell class.
